from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from itertools import combinations

# K_7 has 7 vertices, edges are (i,j) for 0<=i<j<=6
# There are 21 edges.
# We want to avoid monochromatic triangles.
# For each triangle (i,j,k), we add clauses:
# Not all red: ~(x_ij=0 & x_jk=0 & x_ik=0) => x_ij=1 or x_jk=1 or x_ik=1
# Not all blue: ~(x_ij=1 & x_jk=1 & x_ik=1) => x_ij=0 or x_jk=0 or x_ik=0

solver = Glucose3()
edges = list(combinations(range(7), 2))
edge_to_var = {e: i+1 for i, e in enumerate(edges)}

for i, j, k in combinations(range(7), 3):
    e1 = edge_to_var[tuple(sorted((i, j)))]
    e2 = edge_to_var[tuple(sorted((j, k)))]
    e3 = edge_to_var[tuple(sorted((i, k)))]
    # Not all red (0): at least one is 1
    solver.add_clause([e1, e2, e3])
    # Not all blue (1): at least one is 0
    solver.add_clause([-e1, -e2, -e3])

if solver.solve():
    model = solver.get_model()
    print("SAT")
    print(model)
else:
    print("UNSAT")
